summary: Privacy-first analytics for your own sites: a tracker under 2 KB with no cookies, an ingest endpoint that never stores a raw IP, a daily-rotating visitor hash exactly as Plausible defines it, sessions and bounce rate computed at write time, and a fast dashboard. Honest at personal-site scale, and you can state the ceiling.

stack.why: an event is one INSERT; the dashboard is a handful of indexed GROUP BYs
fine to a few million events; say the ceiling out loud
if it needs a bundler it is too big

stack.choice: MaxMind GeoLite2 country database, read locally
stack.why: country from IP without sending the IP anywhere
the ingest endpoint must be public and on HTTPS

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: The site (or sites) you want to measure
prerequisites.why: The tracker is a script tag you add to each site; you need somewhere to add it.
prerequisites.get: Write down each site's domain. Each becomes a site_id in SITES.

prerequisites.name: A MaxMind account and licence key for GeoLite2
prerequisites.why: Country breakdowns need an IP-to-country database. GeoLite2 is free but requires an account to download and to receive updates.
prerequisites.get: Sign up at maxmind.com/en/geolite2/signup, then Account > Manage License Keys > Generate new license key. Download GeoLite2-Country.mmdb (or use geoipupdate). Put the file path in .env.

prerequisites.name: Understand the daily-salt rule
prerequisites.why: The privacy claim rests on one rule: the salt rotates daily and the old one is deleted. If you keep old salts, this is a tracker with extra steps.
prerequisites.get: Read Plausible's data policy page once before Phase 1 so the design is yours, not a guess.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. Sites post to it from the visitor's browser, so it must be public.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: The collector needs an HTTPS address, e.g. stats.yourdomain.com.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: SITES
env.where: Comma-separated site ids accepted by the ingest endpoint. Anything else is dropped.

env.name: GEOIP_DB_PATH
env.where: The MaxMind file from the prerequisites.

env.name: RETENTION_DAYS
env.where: Raw events older than this are rolled up and deleted nightly.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL of the collector, used in the snippet.

phases.title: Identity without cookies
phases.goal: The visitor hash and its salt, done exactly right, before anything else exists.

steps.do: Create the project and the salts table
steps.detail: salts (day, salt, created_at). Generate 32 random bytes per UTC day on first use.
commands: mkdir analytics && cd analytics && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Implement visitorHash(site, ip, userAgent)
steps.detail: sha256(daily_salt + site_domain + ip + user_agent). Include the domain so the same visitor on two of your sites is two hashes. The ip and user agent exist only inside this function.

steps.do: Rotate and delete
steps.detail: At UTC midnight create tomorrow's salt and delete yesterday's row. Deleting is what makes cross-day re-identification impossible even for you.

check: Two calls with the same ip and agent on the same day produce one hash
The same pair on two site ids produce two hashes
After a forced rotation the hash changes and the old salt row is gone
grep of the database file for your own IP returns nothing

phases.title: Ingest endpoint
phases.goal: POST /api/event stores derived facts only and never makes a visitor's page wait.

steps.do: Create the events table with its indexes
steps.detail: events (id, site_id, name, path, referrer_host, screen_class, country, browser, os, visitor_hash, session_id, timestamp). Index (site_id, timestamp) and (site_id, path, timestamp).

steps.do: Derive, then discard
steps.detail: Screen class from a width the tracker sends, browser and os from the user agent, country from the GeoLite2 lookup. Strip query strings and hashes from path. Then drop the inputs.

steps.do: Always answer 202 with an empty body
steps.detail: Unknown site ids are accepted and dropped. Malformed bodies get 202 too. Cap the body at 2 KB. An analytics endpoint must leak nothing about itself.

check: A hand-crafted curl writes one row with no raw identifiers
An unknown site_id returns 202 and stores nothing
A malformed body returns 202 without a stack trace in the log
Country resolves for a known public IP when GEOIP_DB_PATH is set

phases.title: The tracker
phases.goal: Under 2 KB, no cookies, counts SPA route changes once, honours opt-out.

steps.do: Write public/p.js
steps.detail: On load send a pageview with path, referrer and innerWidth via navigator.sendBeacon with a fetch fallback. Hook pushState and popstate for SPA routes. Expose window.plausible-style track(name) for custom events.

steps.do: Respect Do Not Track and a localStorage opt-out flag
steps.detail: If either is set, send nothing at all.

steps.do: Serve it with a long cache header and a version in the filename
steps.detail: p.v1.js; bump on change.

steps.do: Add the snippet to one real site and watch events arrive

check: The minified file is under 2 KB
One page load records exactly one pageview, including under React strict mode
An SPA route change records a second pageview
With the opt-out flag set nothing is sent

phases.title: Sessions and bounce rate
phases.goal: Sessionize at write time so the dashboard never does it.

steps.do: Create the sessions table
steps.detail: sessions (id, site_id, visitor_hash, started_at, last_event_at, entry_path, exit_path, event_count, is_bounce).

steps.do: Join or open a session on each event
steps.detail: If the visitor's last event on this site was under 30 minutes ago, update that session; otherwise open a new one. A session with one pageview is a bounce.

check: Two pageviews 5 minutes apart are one session with is_bounce false
Two pageviews 31 minutes apart are two sessions, both bouncing
Bounce rate matches a hand count on a seeded fixture

phases.title: Bot filtering
phases.goal: Drop obvious bots at ingest and count what you dropped.

steps.do: Filter by user agent and impossible screen classes
steps.detail: A short bot list, plus events with no referrer and a zero width.

steps.do: Count filtered events in a separate table
steps.detail: filtered (day, site_id, reason, n). A traffic drop you can explain beats one you guess at.

check: A curl with a default user agent is filtered
A real browser is not
The filtered count is visible on the dashboard

phases.title: Dashboard
phases.goal: Every panel one indexed query; every number reconcilable with SQL.

steps.do: Build /dashboard behind basic auth with a site switcher
steps.detail: Unique visitors, pageviews, bounce rate and visit duration for today, 7 and 30 days.

steps.do: Add top pages, referrers, countries, browsers, devices
steps.detail: Each a GROUP BY with a LIMIT.

steps.do: Draw visitors per day as inline SVG
steps.detail: No chart library. Dark mode.

steps.do: Seed 100,000 events and time every panel

check: Every number reconciles with a hand-written query on the seeded fixture
The page renders in under 200 ms on 100,000 events
Switching sites changes every panel

phases.title: Retention and deploy
phases.goal: Old events rolled up, live on your domain, documented with the ceiling stated.

steps.do: Write the nightly rollup
steps.detail: daily (day, site_id, visitors, pageviews, bounces) computed from events, then delete events older than RETENTION_DAYS. Charts read daily for old ranges.

steps.do: Add /healthz, systemd, Caddy and a backup command
Write the README and the data policy
steps.detail: The snippet, a plain-language policy (collected, derived, never stored, salt deleted daily), and the traffic ceiling as a number.

check: Retention runs without breaking historical charts
A reader goes from clone to a tracked site using only the README
PRIVACY.md states that the daily salt is deleted

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the collector is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.

steps.do: Lock the box down
steps.detail: Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: An analytics collector you can point several small sites at with a privacy policy you can defend, and a stated scale at which you would move to Plausible itself.

architecture.owns: the daily salt and the hash
architecture.swap: The one module that must not change casually; its test suite is the privacy claim
Any listener writing the same rows
Could move to a batch job; the schema stays
Any UI over events, sessions and daily
Adjust the window; the daily table is the long-term record

operations.backup: SQLite .backup nightly; the daily table is small and is the part worth keeping for years.
operations.restore: Copy back, start, confirm the dashboard totals for last month match the last known figure.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz, and an alert if events per hour drops to zero for a site that normally has traffic.
operations.incident: If raw IPs were ever logged by mistake, delete the log, rotate the salt, and record the incident in PRIVACY.md.

releaseGate: Identity tests pass and the database contains no raw IP or user agent
One restore drill performed and dated

notIncluded: Funnels, goals, revenue attribution and scheduled email reports.
Bot filtering tuned on adversarial traffic. Yours is a list.
Millions of pageviews. SQLite on one box is honest for personal sites; above that, self-host Plausible.
after: A public shareable dashboard link per site
Goal tracking as a custom event with a conversion panel
